evals.prompt: Explain Okta XAA for an enterprise AI agent calling a SaaS resource app on behalf of a user. Correct the phrase 'Extensible Access Architecture,' identify the actors, and trace the token flow without claiming that the user's ID token is accepted directly by the resource API.
evals.expected_output: State that XAA means Cross App Access. Identify the user, requesting app/agent, Okta IdP, resource app authorization server, and resource API. Trace ID token to audience-bound ID-JAG at Okta, then ID-JAG plus requesting-client authentication to a scoped resource-app access token.

evals.prompt: An Okta administrator disables a managed XAA connection during an incident and declares all access revoked immediately. Review the claim and provide containment verification.
evals.expected_output: Explain that disabling the connection blocks new ID-JAG exchanges but existing access tokens are controlled by the resource app and can remain valid. Require short lifetimes, resource-app token/session invalidation, requesting-client disablement or rotation, correlated audit evidence, and tests proving both new exchanges fail and existing access is contained.
